model_fitness.best_available_model: Cdkl5-null mouse (constitutive KO) dosed ICV with a Map1s RNase-H gapmer, read at the level of cortical/hippocampal dendritic morphology, convulsant-threshold EEG and visual evoked potentials (EVIDENCE: the KO's dendritic, EEG-to-convulsant, VEP and Akt/rpS6 phenotypes are published, PMID:24838000); primary Cdkl5-null neurons for the dose-ranging step (EVIDENCE: Map1s lowering rescued microtubule dynamics in exactly this preparation, PMID:30266824).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the proximal node: the KO lacks MAP1S/EB2/ARHGEF2 phosphorylation and shows the microtubule-dynamics defect that Map1s lowering corrects (EVIDENCE, PMID:30266824; PMID:30377159). ICV gapmer delivery reproduces the validated perturbation (dose reduction of MAP1S) rather than an analogue of it (INFERENCE).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partial. Naked ICV/intrathecal gapmers reach forebrain excitatory and inhibitory neurons but on a ventricular-to-deep gradient, so knockdown depth will differ between the cell populations implicated in CDD behaviour (EVIDENCE that both excitatory and inhibitory forebrain neurons matter, PMID:24838000; HYPOTHESIS, not_studied, that a tolerated dose reaches enough of each).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Quantitative: MAP1S protein per region (PD), dendritic arbor complexity, VEP amplitude, PTZ/convulsant EEG threshold. Phospho-EB2 serves only as a negative control here - MAP1S lowering acts downstream of the kinase and should NOT restore it (INFERENCE from PMID:39033321).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Cdkl5-null mice have no spontaneous seizures, only abnormal convulsant responses, so the endpoint families care about most cannot be tested in this model (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:24838000). Non-uniform knockdown means a negative in vivo result is ambiguous between 'wrong mechanism' and 'insufficient coverage' - which is why regional PD must be measured in the same animals.

plan.critical_question: Does partial MAP1S lowering in vivo convert the published microtubule-dynamics rescue into any organism-level benefit in Cdkl5-null mice - and does it do so at a dose that leaves wild-type animals unharmed?
plan.proposed_experiment: Single ICV bolus dose-response of a validated Map1s gapmer (3 doses) versus a control oligonucleotide in Cdkl5-null and wild-type littermates, dosed after phenotype onset (~P30-P45) rather than neonatally, so the result speaks to the post-symptomatic window. Four weeks later, in the same animals: (i) regional MAP1S protein by western/immunoassay in superficial cortex, deep cortex and hippocampus (mandatory - interprets everything else), (ii) phospho-EB2 as a specificity control, (iii) VEP amplitude, (iv) convulsant-threshold EEG, (v) Golgi/sparse-label dendritic arbor quantification in visual and somatosensory cortex. A short preceding in vitro step (graded Map1s knockdown in Cdkl5-null AND wild-type primary neurons, reading microtubule growth-episode length and dendritic transport in both genotypes) sets the target knockdown depth and detects an inverted phenotype in wild-type cells before any animal is dosed.
plan.model: Cdkl5-null mouse plus wild-type littermates (PMID:24838000); primary Cdkl5-null and wild-type cortical/hippocampal neurons for the dose-setting step (PMID:30266824).
plan.primary_readout: Regional MAP1S protein knockdown (PD) paired with VEP amplitude as the primary efficacy endpoint; dendritic arbor complexity and convulsant-threshold EEG as co-primaries.
plan.supportive_result: In regions where MAP1S is lowered 30-60%, VEP amplitude and/or dendritic complexity shift significantly toward wild-type, with a dose-response, while wild-type animals at the same exposure are unchanged and phospho-EB2 stays low (confirming the effect is downstream of the kinase, not off-target CDKL5 restoration).
plan.negative_result: Verified 40-60% MAP1S lowering in deep cortex and hippocampus with no movement in VEP, dendritic arbor or convulsant threshold in nulls - or improvement only at doses that degrade wild-type animals (no therapeutic window).
plan.decision_enabled: Supportive with a window: commit to gapmer lead optimisation and chronic-dosing tolerability; MAP1S becomes a de-risked, genotype-agnostic target. Negative with confirmed PD coverage: stop the MAP1S arm for all modalities - the single-node fix does not carry the phenotype, and resources should move to CDKL5-level or circuit-level approaches. Ambiguous (poor deep PD): the question is delivery, not biology; repeat with a conditional/genetic Map1s reduction before spending further on chemistry.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Paired primary neuron cultures from Cdkl5-null and wild-type littermates, transfected with a graded Map1s siRNA series - the only model that can ask whether a therapeutic window exists (EVIDENCE that this preparation supports Map1s-knockdown rescue of microtubule dynamics, PMID:30266824). No MAP1S-directed RNAi agent and no Map1s/Cdkl5 double-mutant animal was identified (EVIDENCE, contradictory, no agent retrieved).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes, and better than any in vivo model for this particular question: RISC-mediated partial lowering is the exact perturbation, and culture lets knockdown depth be set per well rather than left to a CSF gradient (INFERENCE from PMID:30266824).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partial - mixed cortical/hippocampal cultures contain both excitatory and inhibitory neurons but do not reproduce the intact circuits that generate VEPs or EEG (EVIDENCE that both populations matter in vivo, PMID:24838000).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Microtubule growth-episode length (EB3 comet imaging), dendritic cargo transport, dendritic arborization - all read in both genotypes at matched knockdown depths. PD is MAP1S itself; phospho-EB2 is explicitly not a valid PD marker for this arm (INFERENCE from PMID:39033321).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Cannot address seizures, cognition or the spatial-uniformity failure mode, which is the arm's dominant in vivo risk. In vitro, delivery is solved artificially, so a positive result says nothing about whether CSF-delivered di-siRNA can reach deep cortex at a tolerated dose (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

plan.critical_question: Is there any depth of MAP1S lowering that normalises the Cdkl5-null microtubule and dendritic phenotype while leaving wild-type neurons normal - i.e. does a therapeutic window exist at all?
plan.proposed_experiment: Two-genotype, six-level knockdown matrix: Map1s siRNA titrated to approximately 0, 15, 30, 50, 70 and 90% protein reduction (quantified per condition) in Cdkl5-null and wild-type primary cortical/hippocampal neurons, with a non-targeting siRNA at matched transfection load. Read microtubule growth-episode length by EB3 comet imaging, dendritic cargo transport by live-imaging of a labelled cargo, and dendritic arbor complexity at a fixed timepoint. Plot both genotype dose-response curves on the same axes. Pre-specify the window criterion: at least one knockdown level at which null neurons are statistically indistinguishable from untreated wild-type while wild-type neurons at that same level are indistinguishable from untreated wild-type. Run the matrix once more in human CDKL5-patient-derived neurons if available, since reduced EB2 phosphorylation has been shown in patient-derived neurons (EVIDENCE, PMID:30266824), to check species-transferability of the window.
plan.model: Paired Cdkl5-null / wild-type primary neurons; optional confirmation in CDKL5 patient-derived neurons (PMID:30266824).
plan.primary_readout: Overlaid two-genotype dose-response curves for microtubule growth-episode length, with dendritic arborization as the functional co-readout; MAP1S protein quantified per condition.
plan.supportive_result: A plateau of knockdown depth (plausibly 30-50%) that fully normalises null neurons on both microtubule and dendritic readouts while wild-type neurons remain unaffected - i.e. a defined, reasonably wide window.
plan.negative_result: Wild-type curves degrade at or below the depth that corrects null neurons (window absent or vanishingly narrow), or null dendritic arborization fails to improve at any depth despite corrected microtubule dynamics (the node corrects the proximal readout but not the morphology).
plan.decision_enabled: Supportive: the window value becomes the design specification for the CNS di-siRNA arm, and the programme proceeds to the in vivo gradient question (which is better answered first with a gapmer, where regional PD is easier to titrate). Negative on either axis: stop MAP1S lowering as a therapeutic strategy across oligonucleotide, RNA and small-molecule arms - no delivery chemistry can rescue a mechanism with no window. This single experiment is cheap, needs no new agent, and is the correct gate before any CNS siRNA investment.

model_fitness.best_available_model: No disease model is the bottleneck here. The blocking gap is chemical matter: no MAP1S-directed agent at any stage was identified, and ChEMBL holds no curated mechanism even for CDKL5 itself (EVIDENCE, contradictory, mcp__rp__chembl_target_drugs CDKL5). The nearest usable surrogate is a biochemical/biophysical MAP1S-microtubule binding assay, which would have to be built.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Only indirectly. The validated perturbation is a reduction in MAP1S protein dose (EVIDENCE, PMID:30266824); occupancy-based small-molecule pharmacology does not naturally reproduce a dose reduction, and non-selective microtubule-acting agents would perturb axonal transport and dividing cells system-wide (INFERENCE, contradictory).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: A CNS-penetrant small molecule would in principle reach all forebrain neurons uniformly, including both excitatory and inhibitory populations - the one genuine advantage over CSF-delivered oligonucleotides (INFERENCE, supportive). Moot without a ligandable target.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Microtubule growth-episode length and dendritic arborization in Cdkl5-null neurons would be the screening endpoints (EVIDENCE, PMID:30266824). Phospho-EB2 would NOT move and must not be used as the screen readout (INFERENCE, PMID:39033321).
model_fitness.important_limitations: MAP1S has no reported small-molecule binding site; a degrader requires a binder first. No in vivo proof-of-concept exists that MAP1S lowering improves any organism-level phenotype, so the target is undruggable and un-de-risked simultaneously.

plan.critical_question: Before any chemistry: is MAP1S even ligandable, and is the target worth chemistry at all given that no animal-level benefit of MAP1S lowering has been shown?
plan.proposed_experiment: Do not start a screen. Sequence two cheap gating steps instead. Gate 1 (biology, shared with the other arms): the two-genotype graded Map1s knockdown matrix in Cdkl5-null and wild-type neurons, plus the ICV gapmer in vivo study described for the oligonucleotide arm - genetic lowering answers whether this node carries any phenotype, at a fraction of the cost of hit-finding. Gate 2 (chemistry, only if Gate 1 is positive): a small tractability assessment - recombinant MAP1S microtubule-binding-domain expression, a fluorescence-polarisation or TR-FRET MAP1S-tubulin binding assay, and a focused fragment/DEL pilot or computational pocket assessment to ask whether any pocket exists at the microtubule-binding interface. In parallel, an E3-ligand degrader route is only viable once a MAP1S binder exists, so Gate 2 determines both routes. Explicitly deprioritise the third route (non-selective brain-penetrant microtubule-stabilising agents such as epothilone-class compounds): no CDD-context data was retrieved for these, and their mechanism cannot deliver selective MAP1S occupancy reduction.
plan.model: Gate 1: paired Cdkl5-null/wild-type neurons and Cdkl5-null mice (PMID:30266824; PMID:24838000). Gate 2: recombinant MAP1S-microtubule biochemical assay (to be built; none retrieved).
plan.primary_readout: Gate 1: genotype-resolved dose-response for microtubule dynamics and dendritic arborization, plus in vivo VEP/EEG. Gate 2: existence of a reproducible, saturable small-molecule binding signal at the MAP1S-microtubule interface with a measurable structure-activity relationship.
plan.supportive_result: Gate 1 shows a clear window and in vivo benefit from genetic MAP1S lowering, AND Gate 2 yields confirmed fragment hits with a tractable pocket - only then is a small-molecule or degrader programme justified.
plan.negative_result: Either gate fails: no in vivo benefit from genetic lowering, or no ligandable site and no binder for a degrader. Either outcome kills the small-molecule arm.
plan.decision_enabled: Pre-emptive decision: allocate no chemistry budget now. The validated perturbation is a dose reduction, which oligonucleotide and RNAi pharmacology execute directly and small molecules do not; chemistry should remain gated behind genetic in vivo proof-of-concept. If families or funders are choosing between arms today, the money belongs in the two-genotype knockdown matrix and the ICV gapmer study, not in hit-finding against an unligandable cytoskeletal protein.
